lessons.title: Biosecurity every day
lessons.html:
Biosecurity every day

Biosecurity means stopping germs from getting onto the farm and into the houses. On a poultry farm, this is one of the most important jobs of every worker. A disease like bird flu can kill a whole house of birds.

Coming onto the farm

  1. Come in only through the main gate.
  2. Sign the register if the farm asks.
  3. Go to the change room. Shower if the farm has a shower-in rule.
  4. Put on clean farm clothes and farm boots. Leave your own clothes and shoes in the clean area.
  5. Do not bring food into the houses.

Going into a house

  1. Step into the foot bath with both boots and stand for a moment.
  2. Wash or sanitise your hands.
  3. Put on the house boots or overshoes if the farm uses them.
  4. Close the door behind you.

Working between houses

Follow the order your supervisor gives you. Usually you go to the youngest birds first and the oldest or sick birds last. Never take equipment from one house to another without cleaning and disinfecting it.

The foot bath

The foot bath must have clean disinfectant at the right strength. Change it when it is dirty or as the farm says. Use gloves and follow the label when you mix it. A dirty foot bath does not kill germs.

Keep wild birds and pests out

  • Close doors and curtains.
  • Report holes in nets, walls and roofs.
  • Clean up spilled feed quickly.
  • Do not move rat bait stations; tell your supervisor if bait is finished.

Your own birds

Many farms do not allow workers to keep chickens or other birds at home, because germs can come to the farm on you. Follow the farm's rule.

lessons.title: Cleaning and disinfecting a house
lessons.html:
Cleaning and disinfecting a house

After birds leave a house, the house must be cleaned very well before new chicks come. Germs left in the house can make the new chicks sick.

Safety first

  • Wear overalls, boots, gloves, goggles and a dust mask.
  • Read the label of every chemical. Ask your supervisor if you do not understand.
  • Never mix chemicals.
  • Switch off electricity to equipment before washing, as your supervisor tells you.
  • If chemical gets in your eyes or on your skin, wash with lots of clean water and tell your supervisor. Take the label to the clinic.

The steps

  1. Remove all litter and manure. Take it to the place the farm uses, away from the houses.
  2. Dry clean: brush and blow dust from walls, roof, fans and equipment.
  3. Wash everything with water and soap (detergent): floor, walls, feeders, drinkers, fans. Start at the top and work down.
  4. Rinse and let it dry.
  5. Disinfect with the disinfectant your supervisor gives you, at the right strength.
  6. Clean the water lines as your supervisor shows you.
  7. Fix broken things and report problems.
  8. Rest the house empty for the days the farm says.

Check your work

Look for dirt in corners, under feeders, on fan blades and on ledges. Germs hide in dirt. Your supervisor may check the house or take swabs. If they find dirt, the area must be cleaned again.

Clean the outside too

Cut grass around the house, remove rubbish and clean up feed spills. This keeps rats and insects away.

lessons.title: Looking after bird health
lessons.html:
Looking after bird health

Signs of sick birds

  • Sitting still with fluffed feathers and closed eyes.
  • Not eating or drinking.
  • Coughing, sneezing or noisy breathing.
  • Runny, green, bloody or very watery droppings.
  • Swollen head or eyes, blue comb.
  • Lame or cannot walk.
  • More dead birds than usual.
  • Birds drink less water than yesterday.

If you see these signs, tell your supervisor straight away. If many birds die suddenly, this can be bird flu or Newcastle disease. Tell the supervisor or manager at once. Do not move birds, eggs or equipment out of the house until you are told.

Helping with vaccination

Vaccines protect birds from diseases. Your supervisor or the vet decides which vaccine and how. You may help:

  • Keep vaccines cold in a cooler box. Do not leave them in the sun.
  • For water vaccines, do what the supervisor says about stopping water before, mixing, and the stabiliser. Chlorine kills the vaccine.
  • Walk the birds gently so they all drink.
  • For spray or eye drop vaccines, follow the method you are shown.
  • Write the date, house, vaccine and batch number on the card.

Giving medicine

Only give medicine your supervisor or vet tells you to give, in the amount they say. Write it on the record card. Birds and eggs must not be sold until the waiting time (withdrawal period) is over.

Dead birds

Wear gloves. Pick up dead birds every walk. Put them in the closed bin. Dispose of them the way the farm says. Wash your hands after.

Culling

Very sick or badly hurt birds must be killed quickly and kindly by a trained person. Do not leave them to suffer.

Key points

  • Shower or change, use the foot bath and sanitise hands every time.
  • Work from young birds to old birds.
  • Clean, wash and disinfect a house fully between flocks.
  • Report sick birds and sudden deaths straight away.
  • Keep vaccines cold and record every vaccine and medicine.
